title: Plane mirrors
target: Use the reflection law and locate a virtual image.
criteria: Use equal incidence and reflection angles.
Place the image the same perpendicular distance behind the mirror.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A ray strikes a mirror at 32° from the normal. Which angle convention is being used?
options: From the line perpendicular to the mirror surface.
From any horizontal line regardless of mirror orientation.
cpa.guide: The normal is perpendicular to the surface at the incidence point.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A ray makes 18° with a flat mirror’s surface. What is incidence angle from its normal?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A ray arrives at 37° from a plane mirror’s normal. What is reflection angle from the normal?
cpa.guide: For specular reflection, incidence and reflection angles are equal.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A diagram shows incidence 24° and reflection 66°, both labeled from the normal. What should be corrected?
options: The two angles must add to 90° when both use the normal.
The incidence angle must always be 90°.
Nothing; all angle pairs are allowed.
The reflected angle should be 24° from the normal.
cpa.guide: The law equates the two angles measured from the same normal.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: A candle is 0.75 m in front of a plane mirror. Where is its virtual image?
options: 0.75 m in front of the mirror.
cpa.guide: A plane mirror places the virtual image the same perpendicular distance behind.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: An object is 1.4 m in front of a plane mirror and is moved 0.3 m toward it. What is the new object-to-image separation?
cpa.guide: New object distance is 1.1 m. Image is 1.1 m behind; separation is 2.2 m.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.
